2027-05-08.title: Mar Yohannan Shleeha · St John the Apostle · Saturday after Suloko
readings: Who will separate us from the love of Christ?
The disciple whom Jesus loved; “Follow me!”
2027-05-08.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), after Suloko (the Ascension): the ten days of waiting and prayer for the Holy Spirit before Pentecost. The Panchangam notes that weddings are not celebrated in these days. The Panchangam keeps today the memory of Mar Yohannan Shleeha, St John the Apostle, and the founding of the Congregation of the Daughters of Mary (1938).
2027-05-08.verse: This is the disciple who is testifying to these things and has written them, and we know that his testimony is true.
theo: Today the Panchangam remembers Mar Yohannan Shleeha, St John the Apostle, son of Zebedee and brother of Mar Yaqob, whom the Panchangam remembered on 30 April. He was a fisherman of Galilee, called with his brother from their father's boat; with Peter and James he saw the raising of Jairus' daughter, the Transfiguration and the agony in Gethsemane. The Church's tradition, from St Irenaeus of Lyons in the second century, recognises him as “the disciple whom Jesus loved,” who leaned on the Lord's breast at the Supper and later gave the Church the fourth Gospel while living at Ephesus (Against Heresies III.1.1, in substance). Many Eastern Churches keep his memory on this day in May. The Gospel shows him in the last scene by the lake after the Resurrection. Jesus has just asked Peter three times, “Do you love me?” and told him to feed his sheep. Then “Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them.” Peter asks, “Lord, what about him?” and Jesus answers, “If it is my will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? Follow me!” Each disciple has his own road. Peter will glorify God by a martyr's death; John will remain long, bearing witness. We are not to measure our call against another's. The only question that matters is the one Jesus puts to each of us: will you follow me?

The Gospel ends with John's own seal: “This is the disciple who is testifying to these things and has written them, and we know that his testimony is true.” The beloved disciple is above all a witness. He stood at the Cross when others had fled, he ran to the empty tomb and “saw and believed,” and he recognised the risen Lord on the shore before anyone else: “It is the Lord!” Love made him see. St Paul's words in the Epistle could stand over John's whole life: “Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will hardship, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?” And the answer: “No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.” Nothing in all creation, “neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor rulers, nor things present, nor things to come,” can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord. St Jerome tells that when John was very old at Ephesus and could no longer walk, he was carried into the assembly and would say only, “Little children, love one another.” When asked why he always repeated it, he answered that it was the Lord's command, and if this alone were done, it would be enough (Commentary on Galatians 6:10, in substance). The apostle of love ended as he began, resting on the heart of Christ.

From the Cross Jesus entrusted his Mother to this disciple: “Here is your mother,” and “from that hour the disciple took her into his own home” (John 19:27). It is fitting, then, that today the Panchangam also remembers the founding of the Congregation of the Daughters of Mary, the Mary Makkal, on 8 May 1938 at Marthandam, in the time of the Servant of God Archbishop Mar Ivanios. Like John, the sisters took the Mother of the Lord into their home and their name. For nearly ninety years they have gone to the villages and to the poor in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and far beyond, in mission, teaching, nursing and the care of the forgotten, bearing quiet witness that nothing can separate us from the love of Christ. Thank God today for the sisters you know, pray for vocations to religious life in our Church, and ask Mar Yohannan to teach you his two lessons: to rest on the heart of Christ in prayer, and to take Mary, the Mother of God, into your home. As we wait in these days for the Holy Spirit, we wait as the apostles did, “constantly devoting themselves to prayer” with Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14).
conn: John 13:23 and 21:20: the disciple who reclined next to Jesus at the Supper follows Jesus after the Resurrection; the Church's tradition knows him as John.
John 19:26–27 and Acts 1:14: John took Mary into his home; the apostles waited for the Spirit in prayer with her.
Song of Songs 8:6 and Romans 8:38–39: love is strong as death; nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ.
fathers: John, the disciple of the Lord, who also leaned upon his breast, himself published a Gospel while living at Ephesus in Asia (Against Heresies III.1.1, in substance).

The blessed John, in extreme old age at Ephesus, was carried to the church and said only, “Little children, love one another”; asked why, he replied that this is the Lord's command, and if it alone is done, it is enough (Commentary on Galatians 6:10, in substance).
magis: Mary's union with her Son continued to his death, when he gave her as mother to the disciple: “Woman, here is your son.”
The Blessed Virgin stood by the Cross and was given by the dying Christ Jesus as a mother to his disciple.
In the life of consecrated persons Mary has a special place; she is the example of consecration to the Father and of union with the Son.
outline: Ask: what is that to you? Follow me! Where am I comparing my road with another's?
Point 1 · The disciple whom Jesus loved
Resting on Christ's heart; a witness whose testimony is true.
Paul's hymn of love that nothing can defeat.
Point 3 · He took her into his home
Mary entrusted to John; the Daughters of Mary founded in 1938.

live: Little children, love one another (1 John 4:7)
Do one quiet act of love today for someone in your home who is hard to love.
Pray the Rosary or a Marian prayer together as a family this evening, and pray for the sisters who serve in our Church.
2027-05-08.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you loved Mar Yohannan Shleeha and let him rest on your heart; from the Cross you gave him your Mother, and after your Resurrection you called him to follow you. By his prayers make us witnesses whose testimony is true, convinced that nothing can separate us from your love. Bless the Daughters of Mary and all consecrated women, and give our Church many generous vocations. Teach us to take your Mother into our homes, and to wait with her in prayer for the Holy Spirit. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The beloved disciple leaned on the Lord's breast at the Supper; in the Holy Qurbono we too come close to the heart of Christ and receive the love from which nothing can separate us.

quick: Mar Yohannan Shleeha, son of Zebedee, is known in the Church's tradition as the beloved disciple and the evangelist of the fourth Gospel.
Paul: nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
The Congregation of the Daughters of Mary was founded on 8 May 1938 at Marthandam; like John, its sisters took the Mother of the Lord into their home.
2027-05-08.action: Do one hidden act of love today for someone hard to love.
2027-05-08.question: Am I comparing my road with someone else's, instead of simply following Jesus?
term: The Syriac word for apostle, one who is sent. Our Church names the apostles with this title: Mar Yohannan Shleeha, Mar Yaqob Shleeha, Mar Thoma Shleeha.
kidsaint: St John was a young fisherman whom Jesus called to follow him. At the Last Supper he leaned close to Jesus, and on Good Friday he stayed at the Cross when others ran away. Jesus gave him Mother Mary to take care of. When John was very old, he kept telling everyone: “Little children, love one another.” Lesson: stay close to Jesus, love Mother Mary, and love one another.

family.explain: Today we remember St John, the friend whom Jesus loved. He stayed with Jesus at the Cross, and Jesus gave him his own Mother: “Here is your mother.” John took Mother Mary into his home. St Paul says nothing can ever separate us from Jesus' love, not sadness, not danger, not even death. Today we also thank God for the Sisters called Daughters of Mary, who work for poor people and for Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the Sisters in our parish and our Church, and for young people whom God is calling to serve him.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make Mother Mary feel at home in our family?”

illus: In a village near Marthandam, an old man who had lost his wife and whose sons lived in the city was found one monsoon evening alone in a house with a leaking roof and no food. Two sisters of a religious congregation who visited the sick in that area came by on their rounds. They did not preach. They mended what they could, cooked rice and stayed until he slept. They kept coming every week for two years. When the parish priest later asked him what had brought him back to the Qurbono after decades, he said, “They kept coming. I understood that someone loved me who did not need me.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you loved Mar Yohannan and gave him your Mother. Keep us in your love, from which nothing can separate us. Amen.
share: Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them (John 21:20). What helps me to follow Jesus closely, as John did?
Who will separate us from the love of Christ? (Romans 8:35). What fears make me doubt his love?
Here is your mother (John 19:27). How does Mary have a place in my home and my prayer?
pm.resp: By the prayers of Mar Yohannan Shleeha, keep us in your love, O Lord.
interc: For our Church, that like Mar Yohannan we may be witnesses whose testimony is true.
For the Congregation of the Daughters of Mary and all religious sisters, in thanksgiving for their service, and for new vocations.
For families, that they may take Mary, the Mother of God, into their homes.
For those who feel separated from God's love by suffering, persecution or sin.
For the elderly and lonely, that someone may come to them with the love of Christ.
pm.close: Father, through Mar Yohannan Shleeha you opened to us the mystery of your Word made flesh. Grant that we may understand what he taught, love as he loved, and with Mary the Mother of your Son wait in prayer for the gift of the Holy Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today the Panchangam remembers Mar Yohannan Shleeha, St John the Apostle, whom tradition knows as the disciple whom Jesus loved. He leaned on the Lord's breast at the Supper, he stood at the Cross, and he was the first to recognise the risen Lord on the shore.

In the Gospel Peter sees John and asks: Lord, what about him? Jesus answers: if it is my will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? Follow me! (John 21:21–22). We are not to compare our road with another's. Each of us has one task: to follow Jesus.

St Paul asks: who will separate us from the love of Christ? Hardship, distress, persecution, famine, sword? No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us (Romans 8:35, 37). John lived this. In his old age, St Jerome tells us, he would say only: little children, love one another.

From the Cross Jesus gave his Mother to John, and John took her into his home. Today we also thank God for the Daughters of Mary, founded on this day in 1938, who serve the poor in the name of Mary. Let us take Mary into our homes, and with her wait in prayer for the Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today we remember St John. He was one of Jesus' best friends! At the Last Supper he sat right next to Jesus. On Good Friday, when many friends ran away, John stayed near the Cross with Mother Mary. Jesus said to him, “Here is your mother,” and John took care of her. When John was very old, he kept saying, “Little children, love one another.” Let us say it too, and do it!

intro: Theme: “Who will separate us from the love of Christ?”

On the memory of Mar Yohannan Shleeha and the founding of the Daughters of Mary, in the days of waiting for the Spirit: the beloved disciple, love that nothing can defeat, and the Mother taken into his home.

sub: Resting on the heart of Christ.
“What is that to you? Follow me!”
A witness whose testimony is true.
q: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is strong as death,
God is love, and those who abide in love abide in God, and God abides in them.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes in silent prayer this week simply resting in Christ's love, without asking for anything.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you;
I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand.
points.apply: Write Romans 8:35 on a card and give it to someone who is suffering.

points.h: He took her into his own home
sub: The Mother given from the Cross.
Waiting for the Spirit with Mary.
q: Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing beside her, he said to his mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
points.apply: Pray a Marian prayer as a family each evening until Pentecost, and pray for religious vocations.

concl: Mar Yohannan teaches us to rest on the heart of Christ and to love one another.
Like him and like the Daughters of Mary, we take the Mother of the Lord into our home and wait with her for the Spirit.
2027-05-08.resolve: Follow Jesus without comparing, trust that nothing can separate you from his love, and welcome Mary into your home.
